author: Keystone Today
title: Bucks County man charged with threatening to assault and murder member of Congress
text:
← Back to the wire
Bucks County man charged with threatening to assault and murder member of Congress
A Bucks County man has been charged with threatening a member of Congress following alleged email threats sent earlier this year. Prosecutors say Aaron Michael McComsey faces up to 12 years if convicted but remains presumed innocent pending trial.
Aaron Michael McComsey, 44, of Perkasie, Pennsylvania, was arrested and charged by indictment with two counts of threatening to assault, murder, or kidnap a federal official, according to an Oct. 15 announcement from United States Attorney David Metcalf.
The indictment alleges that on or about August 4, 2026, McComsey knowingly threatened to assault and murder a member of the United States Congress. The threats were allegedly made with the intent to impede, intimidate, and interfere with the congressional representative while engaged in official duties and to retaliate against the member for their performance of those duties.
According to the indictment, McComsey sent emails to the federal official’s office stating: “Aetna dropped me. Medicare doesn't cover drugs. And Medicaid is refusing to pay. I go into withdrawal in 36 hours. After that time, [the official] is no more on this earth. Fix this or he goes bye bye forever.” Additional emails included: “Just tell [the official] I want 6000 dollars for this month's medication costs. He's a millionaire. Let his ass pay for it. I'm so done. That man is finished”; “Can't wait for the next eagle scout graduation. That's his end”; and “I'm coming over there soon if this isn't resolved.”
If convicted on all charges, McComsey faces a maximum possible sentence of 12 years in prison.
The case was investigated by the United States Capitol Police and is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Joseph LaBar. The U.S. Attorney’s Office acknowledged assistance from the Bucks County District Attorney’s Office under District Attorney Joe Khan.
Officials noted that "the charges and allegations contained in the indictment are merely accusations," and stated that every defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.
